Product Highlights

Compact footprint. Autonomous movement.

SAGV0601 is designed for point-to-point material transport where floor space, route flexibility and repeatable internal logistics matter.

60KG

Compact 60 kg Payload Platform

580 × 510 × 600 mm overall size keeps the robot compact while carrying loads up to 60 kg.

NAV

Free + Linear Navigation

Supports free navigation as well as linear navigation along a configured route to match different factory movement logic.

3D

LiDAR + 3D Camera Sensing

Obstacle avoidance uses one LiDAR sensor together with one 3D camera for environment perception.

AUTO

Automatic Recharging

The robot detects low power and returns for automatic charging; manual charging and quick battery replacement are also supported.

Navigation & Mapping

Choose the movement logic that fits the process.

AMRs are typically distinguished from traditional fixed-path AGVs by their ability to navigate using onboard sensing, mapping and dynamic route logic. SAGV0601 supports both free navigation and linear navigation modes.

Mode 01

Free Navigation

Used when the robot needs autonomous movement through mapped factory or warehouse space.

  • Map can be created using a computer, tablet or the built-in display
  • LiDAR + 3D camera support environment perception
  • Suitable for flexible point-to-point material movement
Mode 02

Linear Navigation

Used when the application calls for movement along a defined route.

  • Runs along the configured path
  • Suitable for repeatable line-side transfer loops
  • Can be aligned with structured internal logistics routes
Application Workflow

See how SAGV0601 moves material through production.

This simplified loop illustrates a typical autonomous material-flow task: collect material, deliver it to the production line, transfer work-in-process to the next area, and return for automatic charging.

Typical Material Flow

Pickup → Delivery → Transfer → Auto Charge

The route is configured around the actual factory layout. This visual demonstrates the operating concept rather than prescribing a fixed route.

01
Material PickupCollect bins, kits or WIP materials from a rack or staging point.
02
Line-Side DeliveryMove material to the SMT or assembly line according to the defined task.
03
Process TransferContinue to inspection, packing or another production station.
04
Automatic ChargingReturn to the charging point when the power-management logic calls for recharge.
Typical Applications

Automate short-distance internal material movement.

The compact 60 kg platform is suited to facilities that need repeated transport between warehouse, kitting, line-side and production areas.

01 / SMT

SMT Line Material Delivery

Move reels, feeders, component kits, tooling or WIP materials between storage and line-side areas.

02 / WIP

Work-in-Process Transfer

Transport trays, bins, subassemblies and in-process materials between manufacturing stations.

03 / WH

Warehouse to Production

Support repeatable point-to-point movement from supermarket or warehouse locations to production areas.

04 / KIT

Kitting & Line Replenishment

Use scheduled or task-based material movement for kits and replenishment loads within the 60 kg payload limit.

05 / QA

Inspection & Process Transfer

Move controlled loads between production, inspection, test and packaging processes.

06 / FLEX

Flexible Intralogistics Routes

Use the compact footprint in facilities where material routes need to remain software-configurable rather than tied to one fixed physical guide.

Deployment Workflow

From route planning to production use.

A successful AMR project starts with the real material flow: pickup points, drop-off points, payload, route conditions, charging position and interaction with operators or equipment.

Application Input

Payload, load dimensions, pickup/drop-off points and required transfer frequency.

Map Creation

Create the working map using a computer, tablet or built-in display.

Route Definition

Configure free-navigation destinations or linear navigation routes.

Charging Setup

Define automatic charging position and power-management logic.

Production Deployment

Run the robot in the actual material flow and optimize task timing around the process.
